quizzes.stem: A developer prefers a cheaper model on their own machine. Where is that choice kept?

options.a: `.mcp.json`, which lists the servers used by one project in the repository
options.b: `.claude/settings.json`, which is committed for the whole team of developers
options.c: `CLAUDE.md`, which every session loads before the first prompt is typed
options.d: `.claude/settings.local.json`, which is listed in the ignore file

explanation.d: The table puts "One developer's overrides" in `.claude/settings.local.json`, which is "No, in `.gitignore`".
explanation.b: Ruled out because the file is committed and holds "Team permission rules, default model, hooks, plugins", so the choice would reach the whole team.
explanation.c: Ruled out because `CLAUDE.md` holds "Commands, conventions, the git workflow", and is not a place for a model setting.
explanation.a: Ruled out because `.mcp.json` holds "The MCP servers a project uses".

quizzes.stem: A workflow sends a long instruction string that someone edits whenever results look wrong. What step makes those edits safe?

options.a: Move it to its own file with a version, a changelog entry and a review
options.b: Shorten it so that fewer words are open to change in each separate edit
options.c: Store it in an environment variable so the repository never holds the text
options.d: Let Claude rewrite it every night from the previous day's results alone

explanation.a: The page says to keep "One file per prompt, in the repository", with "A version in the file", "A changelog entry for every change" and "A review of the change".
explanation.b: Ruled out because the page says "A reworded prompt is a behaviour change", and a shorter prompt is still unversioned and unreviewed.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "keys and tokens are read from the environment or from GitHub Secrets", and a prompt needs history, which an environment variable lacks.
explanation.d: Ruled out because a rewrite nobody reviews is the problem: "A review of the change, ideally with a sample of inputs".

quizzes.stem: A pull request adds one entry to the shared settings that allows a new shell command. How should it be reviewed?

options.a: Not at all, because a project permission rule has no effect on others
options.b: Lightly, because settings files hold preferences and not behaviour
options.c: Like a build script, because it changes what runs on every machine
options.d: By Claude alone, because the model wrote the line in the first place

explanation.c: The page says "a line in `.claude/settings.json` that allows a command or enables a plugin changes what runs on every teammate's machine", so such pull requests "deserve the same care as a change to a build script".
explanation.b: Ruled out because such a line "changes what runs on every teammate's machine", which is behaviour and not preference.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the file is committed and shared, so the rule "changes what runs on every teammate's machine".
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Pull requests that touch these files deserve the same care as a change to a build script", with a person deciding.

quizzes.stem: A workflow starts a runner whenever anyone posts anything, and the bill follows the volume. Which line fixes it?

options.a: A longer `timeout-minutes` value on the job that runs the step
options.b: An `if` on the job that tests the comment body for `@claude`
options.c: A larger `--max-turns` value in the arguments of the action step
options.d: A write permission on the contents of the repository for the job

explanation.b: The page says "Without the `if`, a runner starts for every comment in the repository", and the guard is `if: contains(github.event.comment.body, '@claude')`.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the timeout bounds one run and does not stop runs from starting: the page lists it with "workflow-level timeouts to avoid runaway jobs".
explanation.c: Ruled out because "Set `--max-turns` in `claude_args` to limit iterations", which acts inside a run and does not stop one from starting.
explanation.d: Ruled out because write access is a permission and not a trigger filter, and the page says "Grant the least a job needs".

quizzes.stem: A review job should inspect the code and post findings. Which permission set fits?

options.a: Write access to every scope, so the job never fails for a missing grant
options.b: Write access to the contents, so that findings can be committed
options.c: No permissions at all, because comments need no access to the code
options.d: Read access to the contents, plus the token needed for authentication

explanation.d: The page says "A job that only reviews needs `contents: read`", and the review example reads pull requests and issues as well.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the page says "Reading is enough to review", and write access lets a compromised run change the repository.
explanation.c: Ruled out because "A job that only reviews needs `contents: read`", so some access to the code is required.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the page says "Grant the least a job needs", and a grant of every scope is the opposite.

quizzes.stem: A team wants Claude's review to stop a merge until findings are fixed. What does Code Review do?

options.a: It fails the check run whenever a finding is marked important by the review
options.b: It completes its check run as neutral, so branch protection never blocks on it
options.c: It approves the pull request when no finding is marked important at all
options.d: It requests changes from the author on every single finding it posts

explanation.b: The page says "The check run always completes with a neutral conclusion so it never blocks merging through branch protection rules."
explanation.a: Ruled out because the same sentence says the check run "always completes with a neutral conclusion", so it never fails.
explanation.c: Ruled out because findings "don't approve or block" a pull request, and so an empty review is no approval.
explanation.d: Ruled out because findings are posted "as inline comments", and Code Review "so it advises, and a person merges".

quizzes.stem: A team wants its own rules about money handling and generated files applied only when pull requests are checked, and not in ordinary sessions. Which file holds them?

options.a: `CLAUDE.md`, which every session reads before its first prompt
options.b: `REVIEW.md`, read by the agents that examine the diff
options.c: `.claude/settings.json`, which the whole team commits to the repository
options.d: `prompts/CHANGELOG.md`, which lists the prompt versions and their dates

explanation.b: The page says `REVIEW.md` holds "review-only instructions", and that you use it "to say what your team wants flagged, at what severity, and how findings are reported".
explanation.a: Ruled out because `CLAUDE.md` is "shared project instructions that Claude Code uses for all tasks, not just reviews".
explanation.c: Ruled out because the first page gives that file "Team permission rules, default model, hooks, plugins", which are settings and not review instructions.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the changelog explains versions of prompts, and the first page says it must have "A changelog entry for every change" and not review rules.

quizzes.stem: A prompt file is at version 1.2.0, and its changelog's newest heading says 1.1.0. What does a reviewer conclude?

options.a: The edit is unrecorded, because the record and the number disagree
options.b: The prompt is older than its record, so it should be reverted at once
options.c: The number is wrong, because the record always wins out in such a case
options.d: Nothing, because the changelog is only for people to read

explanation.a: The first page says the changelog's "latest heading equals the file's version", so a mismatch means a change nobody recorded.
explanation.b: Ruled out because the rule is only a heading that is "whose latest heading equals the file's version", and it names no age comparison.
explanation.c: Ruled out because the only rule is "whose latest heading equals the file's version", with no winner, so a reviewer asks for the missing entry.
explanation.d: Ruled out because the page says "A reviewer reading the pull request sees what changed and why", which makes it part of the review.

quizzes.stem: A job must start only for a new note that names the bot, and a second note on the same issue must not stop work that is running. Which pair of settings fits?

options.a: A guard on the comment body, with `cancel-in-progress` set to false
options.b: No guard on the comment body, with `cancel-in-progress` set to true
options.c: A guard on the comment body, with `cancel-in-progress` set to true
options.d: No guard on the comment body, with `cancel-in-progress` set to false

explanation.a: The page says to guard the job with `if: contains(github.event.comment.body, '@claude')`, and for an implementation run to "leave it `false` so that a second comment does not kill work in progress."
explanation.b: Ruled out because "Without the `if`, a runner starts for every comment in the repository".
explanation.c: Ruled out because `cancel-in-progress: true` suits a review: "so a new push replaces the review of an outdated commit".
explanation.d: Ruled out because it lacks the guard, and "Without the `if`, a runner starts for every comment in the repository".

quizzes.stem: A team must choose how to run a nightly dependency review that keeps working when nobody's laptop is on, with no workflow in the repository. Which option fits?

options.a: A hook in the settings file that fires after each edit
options.b: A mention workflow that waits for someone to comment
options.c: A routine with a scheduled trigger on Anthropic's cloud
options.d: A subagent in the project folder that starts at midnight

explanation.c: The page says a routine is "a saved Claude Code configuration", with a scheduled trigger, and it runs on cloud infrastructure so it keeps working "while your laptop is closed".
explanation.b: Ruled out because "its job starts only when the comment mentions the bot", and the job here is nightly.
explanation.a: Ruled out because the page lists "Triggers are scheduled (hourly, nightly, weekly, or once)" for routines, and a hook has no schedule and no open session.
explanation.d: Ruled out because "Triggers are scheduled (hourly, nightly, weekly, or once)" belongs to a routine, and a subagent has no clock.
